evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstructions, Middle Chinese reading and component analysis
evidence.text: The entry labels 忘 a phonosemantic compound with phonetic 亡 and semantic 心. In Baxter–Sagart 2014 it gives 忘 *maŋ and *maŋ-s, with Middle Chinese mjang and mjangH; its Zhengzhang section identifies 亡 as the phonetic component and gives 忘 *maŋ and *maŋs. These are reconstructions in named systems, not direct evidence for when the graph was formed. The local Baxter–Sagart rows agree: 亡 MC mjang, OC *maŋ; 忘 MC mjang / mjangH, OC *maŋ / *maŋ-s.

gaps: No securely dated oracle-bone occurrence or evidence that 忘 existed in Shang writing was verified. Search results and the inspected paleographic summary support bronze and later forms, but do not establish the earliest attested graph.

The bronze-form listing includes late Spring and Autumn and Warring States examples, but this pass did not inspect glyph images; no visual claim is made about their exact strokes or possible corruption.
The Shuowen wording is preserved as a quotation through a modern web dictionary; the primary MOE character-variant entry could not be opened, so its fuller citations and variants remain unchecked.

No dated early textual occurrence or ordered sequence of semantic extensions (forget, neglect, omit, miss) was established. Shuowen's gloss 不識也 is evidence for a historical lexicographic gloss, not a chronology inferred from modern dictionary senses.

The dossier's Baxter–Sagart local row for 忘 is *maŋ and *maŋ-s (MC mjang and mjangH). The online tertiary entry reports the same forms, but local repository data are not external evidence. No exact local or external Baxter–Sagart row for 亡 was available in this research packet; the phonetic relationship is supported here by the cited lexicographic/paleographic analysis, while same-system character-to-character comparison remains incomplete.

The local Unihan row supplied for 忘 is wàng, but official click-through verification failed. 亡's official current Mandarin record was also inaccessible, and its local exact row was not supplied. Neither current reading is treated as proof of an ancient relationship.

No evidence was located in this bounded pass for competing corruption theories, a separate whole-graph loan, or the dossier's proposed derivation involving a perfective suffix. Those claims remain unresolved rather than accepted or rejected.

No securely dated oracle-bone example or Shang-era attestation was verified. The accessible paleographic page records later bronze examples, beginning with a late Spring-and-Autumn example, and later script forms; its links to individual inscriptions returned cache misses.

No dated early textual use or documented chronology of semantic extensions such as ‘forget’, ‘neglect’, ‘miss’, and ‘omit’ was established. A lexicographic gloss and current dictionary definitions do not by themselves provide semantic chronology.

No primary inscription image could be opened to examine strokes, variants, or possible graphic corruption. The accessible account supports a 心 semantic plus 亡 phonetic analysis in the listed bronze-to-later forms, but gives no competing corruption theory.

The local Baxter–Sagart rows support a same-system comparison: 亡 *maŋ and 忘 *maŋ / *maŋ-s, with MC mjang versus mjang / mjangH. The secondary entry also names the phonetic role. This does not date the compound or prove a specific historical sound change. Current Mandarin rows are 亡 wáng and 忘 wàng; only 忘’s official Unihan page was accessible.

The dossier’s suggestion that 忘 derives from 亡 with a perfective suffix remains unverified in this bounded research. No independent early attestations establishing separate source-word and borrowed-word histories were inspected; no whole-graph borrowing account is established here.

The selected seal-script image is a modern vector redraw of a historical script style, not an ancient artifact photograph. Its exact direct image URL is known from the Commons page, but image retrieval failed in this research tool; pixel inspection is left to the downstream image review.

No securely dated oracle-bone occurrence or Shang-era attestation of 忘 was verified. The accessible paleographic summary begins its listed 忘 examples with later bronze material; that does not prove the graph first arose then.
No primary inscription image was inspected, so the exact stroke development, individual graphic variants, and any possible corruption remain unassessed.
No dated textual attestations were established to order the glosses ‘forget’, ‘neglect’, ‘miss’, and ‘omit’; do not infer that semantic chronology from the Shuowen gloss or modern Unihan definitions.

The perfective-suffix proposal reported by Wiktionary remains unresolved: this pass did not inspect the cited scholarly argument or establish separate, dated histories of 亡 and 忘 as spoken words. No independent whole-graph borrowing analysis was found.

Modern Mandarin wàng and wáng were verified in Unihan. Similarity of the historical readings is supported by the supplied same-system Baxter–Sagart rows and the cited phonetic analysis; modern readings alone do not establish the ancient relationship.

The review-requested current Mandarin comparison is supported by the provided exact local Unihan rows (亡 wáng; 忘 wàng) and local Baxter–Sagart rows (亡 OC *maŋ, MC mjang; 忘 OC *maŋ / *maŋ-s, MC mjang / mjangH). Those local files are not external evidence. Both official character-specific Unihan URLs were attempted but inaccessible in this run, so the exact current readings remain without verified official click-through evidence here.

No primary source establishing the proposed derivation of 忘 from 亡 with a perfective suffix was verified; no independent, dated attestations of the proposed source-word and suffixed use were examined. Treat that proposal as unresolved.

The seal-style 忘 image is an explicitly modern digital redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph; no visual inspection of its pixels was performed. Its description page provides identity, source attribution, direct original-file link and reuse statement, but its direct image URL could not be opened in the web tool.

No verified evidence in this follow-up establishes the earliest attested 忘 graph, a dated semantic-extension sequence, or a competing corruption analysis. The dossier’s earlier paleographic summary remains secondary and does not establish an oracle-bone occurrence.
